newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold treading on shaky territory.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold treading on shaky territory.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold looks technically weak, with heavy bands of resistance above and critical support -- the 1993 low of $325.10 -- beckoning on the downside, chartists said.
Platinum may hold out for a short term correction to the upside while silver is under pressure near key $4.60 support.
GOLD - Prices are edging closer to initial support for gold between $332.00 and $333.00, after which gold is vulnerable to further steep losses, technical analysts said.
"Gold has fallen to four-year lows and continues to look weak. The chart is dominated by a seven-month downtrend which comes through today at $341.00," said Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Any rallies would find quite dense resistance up to the downtrend line, as well as at $336.15, the previous low from February this year.
But a break to the downside will find little to keep prices from sinking to critical support levels, she added.
"Below $332 there's nothing until $325.10, the 1993 low which is the lowest it's been in 11 years," Jones said.
In the near term, some dealers expected gold to drift sideways ahead of Tuesday's and Wednesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
Gold had come under pressure in recent days from commodity fund selling against a background of a strong U.S. dollar and stock market.
At 0835 GMT spot gold was quoted at $333.50/$333.80 an ounce, down $0.20 from Monday's New York closing level.
SILVER - Further downside probes are likely on the cards for silver, Jones said, noting it has tested the important $4.60 support area six times in past seven months.
"It's under pressure and if it breaks below $4.59 it's vulnerable to a fall to $4.33," the low from March 1995, she said.
If it holds above $4.59, prices will nevertheless struggle to go above $4.70.
At 0835 GMT silver was indicated at $4.64/$4.66 an ounce, up just once cent from Monday's New York finish.
The gold/silver ratio was currently around 72 percent, having recovered to over 70 percent last week. Having successfully held sideways, it could now test the top of the range at 73.50, Jones said.
PLATINUM - Prices could be gearing up for a short-term upwards correction as long as platinum holds above its uptrend line of the past several months which is currently at $405.40, Jones said.
Resistance is at $440 and then at $451.50, a 50 percent retracement from the last downward move.
The platinum/gold spread, currently at 96.30, was widening out and looks set to test interim resistance at 112, which if broken targets 135, Jones added.
Prices were last quoted at $430.00/$435.00 an ounce, compared to Monday's $423.00/$426.00. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
